canonical.name: Measurability of Holm rejection events
canonical.reason: The local lemma supplies the measurable rejection events needed to define the FWER probability under the page's statistical experiment.

sources.title: Gary W. Oehlert, A First Course in Design and Analysis of Experiments
sources.locator: Chapter 5, Sections 5.1–5.2, printed pp. 79–83 / PDF pp. 99–103: familywise and strong familywise error rates, Bonferroni, Holm, family choice, and Example 5.3.

contents.name: Familywise and strong familywise error rates; distinction from simultaneous confidence intervals
contents.reason: The theorem defines FWER for every true-null configuration and the page states that this rejection guarantee is not a simultaneous-interval guarantee.

contents.name: Bonferroni cutoff for a fixed family of hypotheses
contents.reason: The example computes the one-step threshold on the same four-member family without importing a separate error-control theorem.

contents.name: Holm step-down thresholds and stop-at-first-failure rule
contents.reason: The algorithm records the inclusive rank thresholds and the prefix rejection convention, with a deterministic tie rule.

contents.name: Family selection in Example 5.3
contents.reason: The theorem fixes its family before observation and the page warns that post-data family selection is outside the stated validity assumptions.

contents.name: Example 5.3: sensory characteristics of cottage cheeses
contents.reason: The empirical cheese comparison and its grouping choices are not part of this model-neutral worked arithmetic example for a fixed four-hypothesis family.

contents.name: Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate procedure
contents.reason: This pair proves FWER control for Holm only; it makes no FDR claim and does not import the separate independence assumptions of the step-up procedure.

sources.title: Jelle J. Goeman and Aldo Solari, The sequential rejection principle of familywise error control, The Annals of Statistics 38(6) (2010)
sources.locator: Theorem 1 and complete proof, PDF pp. 4–5; Section 3, Holm specialization and monotonicity/single-step check, PDF p. 9.

contents.name: Theorem 1: sequential rejection principle and induction proof of strong familywise error control
contents.reason: The local theorem proves the finite Holm specialization directly by the earliest true-null rank and union bound rather than assuming this general principle.

contents.name: Bonferroni–Shaffer finite-union bound for true-null p-values
contents.reason: The local theorem applies the authored Bonferroni control to the fixed true-null subfamily after proving the Holm-specific event inclusion.

contents.name: Holm critical-value specialization α_H(R)=α/|H\R|
contents.reason: For an ordered finite family this critical-value rule is exactly the rank cutoff α/(m−j+1) in the local procedure.

contents.name: P3 and S2 procedures for logically related hypotheses
contents.reason: The assigned claim is ordinary unweighted Holm for arbitrary dependence; the logical-relationship procedures require extra structure and are not asserted here.

sources.title: John K. Hunter, Measure Theory lecture notes
sources.locator: Chapter 1 §1.5, printed pp. 4–5 / PDF pp. 4–5; Chapter 3 §§3.1–3.2, printed pp. 33–36 / PDF pp. 36–39: sigma-algebra closure, measurability by preimages, threshold sets, and arithmetic operations.

contents.name: Definition 3.1 and Proposition 3.2: measurable maps and the preimage criterion
contents.reason: The local measurability proof applies the preimage definition to the finite cells defining each Holm rejection event.

contents.name: Proposition 3.5: real-valued measurability characterized by threshold sets
contents.reason: The local lemma checks that comparison and cutoff events are preimages of Borel half-lines.

contents.name: Proposition 3.6: arithmetic operations preserve measurability
contents.reason: The local proof writes p_i-p_j as a sum with a scalar multiple and uses its measurability for comparisons.

contents.name: Section 1.5: closure properties of sigma-algebras
contents.reason: The local proof uses finite intersections to form ordering cells and finite unions to form each rejection event.
